events.title: Marie Antoinette Marries the Future Louis XVI
events.description: At just 14, the Austrian archduchess Marie Antoinette married the 15-year-old heir to the French throne, Louis, in a lavish ceremony. The marriage was meant to seal an alliance between the Habsburgs and the Bourbons.
events.significance: The union tied her to the French crown. Two decades later she became one of the best-known figures of the French Revolution.

events.title: Senate Fails to Convict President Andrew Johnson
events.description: In his impeachment trial, 35 of 54 senators voted to find President Andrew Johnson guilty over his attempt to dismiss Secretary of War Edwin Stanton. That was one vote short of the two-thirds majority needed to remove him.
events.significance: Johnson stayed in office. The narrow result set a lasting precedent for how high the bar is for removing a U.S. president.

events.title: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising Ends
events.description: After almost a month of fighting, German forces crushed the Jewish resistance in the Warsaw Ghetto and blew up the Great Synagogue. Poorly armed fighters had held out far longer than their occupiers expected.
events.significance: The uprising became a lasting symbol of courage and defiance against Nazi persecution.

events.title: China Launches the Cultural Revolution
events.description: Mao Zedong's movement began with a drive to purge supposed counter-revolutionaries from Chinese society and the Communist Party. It grew into a decade of upheaval.
events.significance: The Cultural Revolution caused widespread persecution and loss of life. It also disrupted education and culture, and it reshaped modern China.

events.title: Junko Tabei Becomes the First Woman to Summit Mount Everest
events.description: Japanese mountaineer Junko Tabei reached the top of the world's highest peak. She went on to climb the highest mountain on every continent.
events.significance: Her climb broke a major barrier in mountaineering and inspired generations of women climbers.
